deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.60): K is a category with finite limits (the 'ambient' category, e.g. sets or topological spaces). A 'tame structure' is a pair (M, φ) where φ: M → K is exact (preserves finite limits), conservative and hence faithful, and M has an object I_0 such that every object of M embeds into some power I_0^n. Up to equivalence, such data amount to an object I of K together with, for each n, a family M_n of subobjects of I^n. These families must be stable under finite intersections and under inverse images by 'simplicial' maps I^m → I^n (coordinate maps). They must also be stable under images by simplicial maps whenever the map is mono on the subobject (condition 3°). In model-theoretic terms this is a 'structure' of definable sets on I, with existential quantification allowed only along injective projections. Condition (3' bis) allows all projections. Condition 4° asks two things: (a) each M_n is stable under finite sups; (b) there is a tame monomorphism e ⊔ e → I, i.e. two distinct tame points.

This page, first paragraph: 4° is equivalent, in terms of (M, φ), to two conditions. (a) M has finite disjoint sums and φ preserves them. (b) There is a mono e_M ⊔ e_M → I_0. This is the standard device of realising X ⊔ Z ⊂ I^n inside I^{n+1} as X×{p} ∪ Z×{q} using two distinct points p, q. Conversely, coproducts preserved by φ give finite unions of subobjects.

(D) Assume K has pushouts X ⊔_Y Z whenever Y → X and Y → Z are mono. Take an arbitrary f: Y → X. By the factorisation hypothesis (B), f = (image inclusion) ∘ (effective epi). Since the first factor is epi, the cokernel pair of f equals that of the image inclusion, so X ⊔_Y X exists. Next, f is epi iff the codiagonal ∇: X ⊔_Y X → X is an iso. Hence, if M has the same types of pushouts and φ preserves them, conservativity gives: φ(f) is epi iff f is epi. Further transfers from K to M follow:
- If epi ⇒ effective epi in K, then likewise in M. This needs the descent-of-tameness condition in the p.60 margin.
- If every mono is effective in K, then likewise in M, since φ preserves equalisers and these cokernel pairs.

Then the construction problem. Given tame X ← Y → Z with tame monos i, j, one wants a pushout in M preserved by φ. That is, one must put a tame structure on the K-pushout X ⊔_Y Z such that X → X ⊔_Y Z and Z → X ⊔_Y Z are tame and the universal property holds in M. The final diagram presents X ⊔_Y Z as the coequaliser of Y ⇉ X ⊔ Z, i.e. a quotient of the coproduct obtained in the first paragraph.

The next page continues with stronger hypotheses on K: pushouts of monos are monos and the squares are cartesian (adhesive-type conditions). It reduces existence to finding a cartesian square of tame monos into some tame S'. It then introduces I_0 injective (5°) and every subobject being a zero-set f^{-1}(0_n) (6°).

Overall purpose: a categorical axiomatics of 'tame topology', i.e. categories of definable/semi-analytic-type sets, and of which finite colimits such categories carry.
errors: 'on en peut remplacer f par l'inclusion de son image' tacitly uses the effective-epi/mono factorisation of (B) and that the epi part does not change the cokernel pair; correct, but it relies on (B).

'kif kif dans M' for epi ⇒ effective epi is not automatic from exactness plus conservativity. One also needs that the K-coequaliser of the kernel pair is a coequaliser in M, which is supplied by the margin condition of p.60 (if h∘q is tame with q an effective epi, then h is tame). The page does not restate this.
No genuine mathematical error otherwise; the epi ⇔ codiagonal-iso criterion and its transfer via a conservative pushout-preserving functor are correct.

ideas.what: Finite coproducts in the category of tame/definable objects are equivalent to closure of each M_n under finite unions plus existence of two distinct tame points (mono e⊔e → I_0).
ideas.modern_name: Definable disjoint unions via two distinct constants (category of definable sets is extensive / has coproducts)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in model theory (definable sets, elimination of imaginaries context; e.g. van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures', 1998)

ideas.what: f is epi iff the codiagonal of its cokernel pair is an iso; a conservative functor preserving these pushouts reflects and preserves epis, and transfers 'epi ⇒ effective epi' and 'mono ⇒ effective mono'.
ideas.modern_name: Cokernel-pair characterisation of epimorphisms; reflection of properties by conservative exact functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard category theory (dual of kernel-pair criterion for monos)
ideas.where_published: Similar arguments in SGA 4 Exposé I, but not this specific statement

ideas.what: Tame structures as pairs (M, φ: M → K) with φ exact and conservative and every object embedding in I_0^n, studied by asking which finite colimits (coproducts, pushouts along monos) lift to M.
ideas.modern_name: Categorical axiomatisation of o-minimal/definable structures (category of definable sets as a lex/regular/extensive category over Set)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries (1984), Pillay–Steinhorn (1986), Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn; categorical logic of definable sets: Makkai–Reyes (1977)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984) only announces tame topology programmatically, without this categorical formalism

ideas.what: Pushouts along monos as coequalisers of Y ⇉ X⊔Z; seeking a tame structure on them (continued next page with 'pushouts of monos are mono and cartesian').
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lack–Sobociński (adhesive categories, 2004); gluing of definable sets in o-minimal geometry (definable spaces, van den Dries)

missed.claim: In 1974 Grothendieck formulates tame topology as a functor M → K (exact, conservative, every object embedding in I_0^n). The equivalent data are a sequence of families M_n of subobjects of I^n with closure axioms, which is precisely the later model-theoretic notion of a 'structure' underlying o-minimality. On this page he translates closure properties (finite unions, two points) into categorical properties of M (finite disjoint sums preserved by φ). This dictionary between definable-set axioms and categorical exactness properties anticipates o-minimality by about a decade, and is not recorded as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: Cela équivaut, en termes des (M,φ), à la condition que l'on ait a) Dans M les sommes disjointes finies existent, et φ y commute b) ∃ monomorphisme e_M ⊔ e_M → I_0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's tame-topology programme had a concrete categorical axiomatics in 1974, ten years before the Esquisse. That is relevant to the history of o-minimality and to current categorical treatments of definable sets and tame geometry.

missed.claim: He sets up the problem of lifting pushouts along monos from K to the tame category M. The next page identifies conditions very close to the adhesive-category axioms (pushouts of monos are mono, the square is cartesian, monos effective, pushouts universal). The existence criterion for tame pushouts (a cartesian square of tame monos into a tame S') is left open; no theorem on gluing of tame structures is reached.
missed.quote: on cherche X ⊔_Y Z dans M avec φ y commutant. Donc on doit définir une structure modérée sur X ⊔_Y Z au sens de K ... et que ça satisfasse la P[ropriété] universelle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gluing definable sets along definable subsets underlies definable spaces and o-minimal homotopy theory. A categorical (adhesive-type) criterion for when a tame structure admits such pushouts is a natural question that this thread poses explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual arguments on this page are routine category theory. Historically, though, the page belongs to a 1974 categorical axiomatisation of tame/definable structures predating o-minimality. Its pushout-along-mono analysis anticipates adhesive-category conditions. This is a notable unpublished detail but not a new theorem.

'si dans M les = types de sommes amalgamées existent' → '=' is Grothendieck's shorthand for 'mêmes': 'les mêmes types de sommes amalgamées'.
'alors on a[?] φ(f) est un épi ssi f l'est' → 'alors φ(f) est un épi ssi f l'est'.
'i.e. d'objets modérés (et [-K-])' with insertion → 'On considère un diagramme dans M, i.e. d'objets modérés et de morphismes modérés'.
